types.name: RMissileStreak

fields.name: numPoints
fields.comment: high: ctor 0xed310 zeroes; Update(COORD4&) 0xa0ea0 caps it at 0x60 and adds 2 every other frame, indexes points[] by it; Draw 0xa1330 needs >3; PS2 +0x0 in both ctors/Reset/Update/Draw. Name invented

fields.name: frameCount
fields.comment: high: Update() 0xa0e90 is just 'INC [ECX+0x4]'; Update(COORD4&) tests its low bit and increments; Draw uses it for the start index; PS2 Update 0x1e43e0 same. Name invented

fields.name: streakType
fields.comment: high: indexes float tables 0x1c4b00/0x1c4b0c and the static renderer table 0x201250[3] in Update/Draw; Missile ctor writes 1/2 here (Missile+0xa8); PS2 ctor RMissileStreak(StreakType) 0x1e4218 stores its arg at +0x8

fields.name: points
fields.comment: medium: Update writes 16-byte records at this+0x10+i*16 (LEA EDI,[ESI+0x10]; +0x14/+0x18 floats); Draw passes this+(start+1)*16 to the renderer; PS2 Update LEAs +0x10/+0x14/+0x18. Count 100 fills the 0x650 gap (numPoints max 0x61). Name invented

types.comment: Missile/grenade smoke streak: a count, a frame counter, a streak type and a ring of up to 100 COORD4 points. NO vptr and NOT an RAutonomousObj subclass (ctor 0xed310 only zeroes +0/+4/+8; Update reads +0 as a count). Embedded at Missile+0xa0 and Grenade+0x70; size = gap to the next field in both (0x650 = 0x10 + 100*16). Same offsets on PS2 (no vptr there either)

types.comment: proximity mine; FastFree 0x88. Ctor uses the SimpleRigidBody PhysicsObject ctor 0x6f190 (type 5) and news an RAutonomousObj (0x80, vtable 0x18a398 stored inline) as its render object via SetRenderObject 0x6f3f0. PhysicsObject vptr is at PS2 +0x68, so Mine's own fields share offsets on both builds; PS2 bools +0x7c/+0x84 are 4 bytes but padded, no shift

types.comment: hit-scan bullet; FastFree 0xe0. Own vptr (1 slot, deleting dtor), no base. PS2 keeps the vptr LAST (+0xcc, ctor/dtor), and Xbox pads its vptr to 0x10 (16-byte vector members), so every field is PS2+0x10. The ctor fires the ray (CollideWithObjects/CollideWithWorld/Fire loop) and ends by calling its own deleting dtor: instances never outlive construction
